🟠 [gate-exit0-masks-bare-form] MUST-FIX The new recognizer strips every `exit 0` line before taking the last command and then matches a regex that accepts BOTH the bare `[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]` and the `[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1` forms, so a suite ending `[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]` followed by `exit 0` is classified as finalizing even though the trailing `exit 0` masks the failure (the bare form's status never propagates). Impact: the gate would pass an always-green suite, exactly the class it exists to catch; no fixture covers this shape. Smallest remediation: in `finalizes()` take the last non-blank line L and the one before it P; accept if L matches `^\s*\[ "\$\{?FAIL\}?" -eq 0 \](\s*\|\|\s*exit 1)?\s*$`; otherwise accept only if L matches `^\s*exit 0\s*$` AND P matches the `|| exit 1` form (not the bare form); add negative fixture `ownexit0` (`[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]` then `exit 0`) to the reject loop and record its red line.
🔵 [rollover-postcondition-pass-count] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `vacuous_exit` is only reachable at the three precondition sites, so the SKIP line itself cannot be emitted by a real run; but the suite's own final summary (outside this diff) is not shown to guard `PASS -gt 0`, so a post-precondition run that calls neither ok() nor bad() would still print `0 passed, 0 failed` green. Excluded: not a change the spec asked for and no evidence such a path exists after the graph check; a one-line `[ "$PASS" -gt 0 ] || bad "no assertion executed"` before the summary would close it.
🔵 [rollover-runsh-skip-surfacing] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The hand chose the SKIP route (stdout+stderr `SKIP [mission-terminal-rollover] ...`, exit 0) rather than a hermetic precondition, citing the ~20 validator predicates; whether run.sh actually surfaces that exact line in its summary is not demonstrated in the diff. Excluded: spec permits the SKIP option and the line matches the requested `SKIP [suite] <reason>` shape; confirm with a grep of `SKIP` in run.sh in the landing report.
